properties.name: An assumption is recorded as something that can stop being true, and what rests on it is computed
properties.statement:
NOT FROM reflow. Raised 2026-07-28 from ordinary architecture and risk practice, after Anthony's instruction to bring judgement rather than treat reflow's workflows as canon. reflow had no equivalent either; this is a gap in both.

Designs rest on things believed true about the world that nobody controls, and those beliefs are what actually break architectures. reflow2 has no way to say so. Constraint BINDS (a limit the design must respect, and it is enforced). Decision records a choice with rationale (why WE chose, not what we BELIEVED). RISKS and MITIGATES describe something that might go wrong and what reduces it. None of them expresses "this design is sound ONLY WHILE X remains true, and X is not ours to decide" — which is a different object with a different lifecycle: an assumption is not enforced, not chosen, and not a risk to be reduced. It is a proposition that is checked, and that can be INVALIDATED, at which point everything resting on it needs revisiting.

THE MISSING COMPUTATION IS THE POINT, not the node type. Once an assumption is a node with things hanging off it, "assumption X no longer holds" becomes a propagate query with a real answer: these four capabilities and this interface were justified by it. Today that reasoning exists only in prose inside Decision rationale, where nothing can walk it. reflow2 already has every mechanism this needs — propagate_change computes blast radius, cap:freshness says when a claim was last confirmed, DriftEvent records a divergence against reality, and the Verification machinery already distinguishes proof against a model from proof against reality (cap:evidence-fidelity). An assumption is the node those mechanisms are missing.

WHY IT MATTERS PARTICULARLY IN THIS OPERATING CONTEXT. Several organisations, competing partially-built designs, coupled repositories each with its own graph, work delivered as increments. Almost everything load-bearing about the OTHER organisation's system is an assumption: that their interface will not change before your increment lands, that their component means what its name says, that the version they run is the version they declared. req:version-combination-is-an-object pins the versions; nothing records WHY a pinned combination was believed safe or what breaks when it stops being. Evolving a ten-year-old production stack on the fly is the same shape: most of what a change rests on is a belief about code nobody has read recently.

DISTINGUISH FROM WHAT EXISTS, because the boundary is what makes it useful: a Constraint that is violated is a defect in OUR design; an assumption that fails is a change in the WORLD, and the honest response is different — not fix the build, but revisit what was justified by it. Also distinct from a KPP (req:inviolable-intent), which is intent we refuse to weaken; an assumption is a fact we do not control.

OPEN and not decided: whether this is a new node type or Constraint gaining a kind that separates binds-us from believed-of-the-world (the second is cheaper and risks blurring the very distinction that makes it worth having); what edge carries "rests on" (DEPENDS_ON is lateral and already crowded; a dedicated relation may be clearer); and whether an assumption can carry an expiry or a confirmation cadence, which cap:freshness already models for claims and would make "nobody has checked this in six months" computable rather than remembered.
